Owen Patel: FYI alert group - DCGM exporter in eu-west is spiking Xid 63 across several nodes, Prom alert fired for high xid error score. Link: https://deploy.prod/alerts/2350011223 :eyes:
Infra Bot: ALERT: dcgm_gpu_xid_score_high on cluster-eu-west - affected_nodes=3, severity=warning, alert_id=2350011223
Maya Chen: How widespread? which racks/region/instance type? MIG or mons?
Owen Patel: 3 nodes in eu-west-1b (gpu-a100-sxm), not MIG. Errors concentrated on PCIe bus 1 on each card. No large regen yet, but repeated Xid 63 bursts last 20m.
Li Wang: Quick triage: 1) cordon+drain one of the affected nodes, 2) collect nvmes, dmesg, and dcgm exporter logs, 3) capture GPU ECC counters and pci errors. Commands: `kubectl drain node/gpu-eu-1b-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` and `sudo dcgmi dmon --show-errors` and `journalctl -u dcgm-exporter -o short -n 500`.
Samir Rao: Re: the Prom rule, current simple rate windows are noisy. Proposal: compute a weighted "consecutive XID score" that gives extra weight to repeated Xid spikes on the same GPU across narrow windows, and then aggregate per-node. Example PromQL (prototype):
```
# per-gpu recent spikes
gpu_spikes = increase(dcgm_gpu_xid_events_total{error_code="63"}[5m])
# short-window multiplier for repeat bursts
short_spikes = increase(dcgm_gpu_xid_events_total{error_code="63"}[1m])
# score = 1*5m + 3*1m to bias recent rapid repeats
gpu_score = gpu_spikes + 3 * short_spikes
node_score = sum by(node)(gpu_score)
```
Then alert when `node_score > 8` for 3/5 minutes. This reduces single-shot noise but catches rapid repeats.
Maya Chen: Nice. Can we also bias away from transient host reboots and focus on card-local counters? i.e., prefer ECC counters over generic docker restarts.
Samir Rao: Yes - filter metrics where `device_error_origin="gpu"` and prefer `dcgm_ecc_corrected` / `dcgm_ecc_uncorrected` increases as tie-breakers. Also add a clause to ignore nodes with ongoing driver restarts: `absent(up{job="nvidia-driver"})` or a `driver_restarts` metric.
Owen Patel: If we change the rule, what's the risk of delaying real failures? some failures need immediate drain.
Li Wang: We can keep a fast-path alert: if single-gpu `increase(dcgm_gpu_xid_events_total[1m]) >= 15` then escalate immediately and auto-cordon. The weighted rule is for noisy but persistent cases.
Maya Chen: Operational step: temporarily divert traffic off nodes with node_score >= 10 using pod anti-affinity / scheduler class to route to spare pool. We have spare capacity in eu-west-standby.
Samir Rao: For automation, we add a scoring hook in alertmanager template that returns a `drainSuggested=true/false` label based on thresholds, and an infra-runbook link. Example alert rule snippet to deploy:
```
- alert: DCGMNodeWeightedXidHigh
  expr: |
    sum by (node) (
      increase(dcgm_gpu_xid_events_total{error_code="63"}[5m])
      + 3 * increase(dcgm_gpu_xid_events_total{error_code="63"}[1m])
    ) > 8
  for: 3m
  labels:
    severity: warning
    drainSuggested: "true"
  annotations:
    runbook: https://infra.internal/runbooks/gpu-xid-weighted
```
Maya Chen: Also add a cooldown for flapping: after a node is auto-drained, suppress the alert for 30m to avoid repeated actions.
Owen Patel: Good. For RMA decisioning, what threshold are we comfortable with?
Li Wang: Recommend this playbook: compute cumulative node_score over 6 hours; if cumulative >= 60 AND there are nonzero increases in `dcgm_ecc_uncorrected` -> open RMA. Short checklist in ticket: last 3 drain logs, dmesg, nvlink errors, thermal history.
Samir Rao: I'll push a staged Prom rule to canary region and link the PR here. Also will add the immediate fast-path rule for single-gpu flood >=15 in 1m to keep correctness.
Owen Patel: Thanks — can you also add a log-collector step to the runbook so on drain we snapshot `/var/log/nvidia/*` and `/var/log/kern.log`?
Li Wang: Added to the runbook snippet: `tar -czf /tmp/gpu-triage-$(date +%s).tgz /var/log/nvidia /var/log/kern.log /var/log/dcgm-exporter` and upload to incident bucket.
Owen Patel: OK will roll the canary tonight and manually drain the two worst nodes after the patch. Thanks everyone :heart:
Maya Chen: TY! keep me posted, ping @oncall if it escalates. :thumbsup:
Infra Bot: NOTE: automated canary job scheduled at 23:45 UTC — job id canary-2350011223
Owen Patel: Acknowledged.
